caseName: New York, New Haven & Hartford Railroad v. United States
caseNameFull: NEW YORK, NEW HAVEN & HARTFORD RAILROAD COMPANY v. United States
syllabus: A railroad after accepting and transporting without protest a shipment of gold in mail sacks consigned by the Treasury Department, and after receiving the amount fixed by readjustment for carrying mail matter under its contract therefor, has no claim for additional pay for carrying the gold and attendant railway mail guards, whether the shipment was properly mail matter and the requirements of the statute concerning postal service were technically complied with or not.
summary: Judgment was rendered in favor of the United States in the court below. On appeal the judgment was affirmed, and the Supreme Court decided:

opinions.author: Holmes
opinions.text:
Mr. Justice Holmes

delivered the opinion of the Supreme Court February 27, 1922.
